UV light purification system installed near the indoor coil

UV light purification systems are designed to support cleaner HVAC operation by helping reduce certain biological buildup on compatible components. These systems are often installed near the indoor coil or air handler, where moisture and organic buildup can become a concern.
UV lights can help limit buildup on certain indoor HVAC components, supporting cleaner system operation.
As part of a broader IAQ strategy, UV purification may help address certain odor and air cleanliness concerns.
Proper placement is important. Our technicians help determine whether a UV system fits your HVAC setup.

Indoor purification systems help reduce airborne particles moving through your home. Unlike portable units that treat one room at a time, whole-home air purification solutions can work with your HVAC system for broader coverage. A good option for homes dealing with dust, pet dander, pollen, odors, or general air quality concerns.
Whole-home air purifier integrated with the HVAC system
Indoor purification systems can support cleaner air throughout the home when properly matched to your HVAC system.
Purification can help reduce airborne particles that contribute to dust buildup, allergy-like symptoms, and lingering smells.

settings.title: Which Indoor Air Quality Solution Is Right for Your Home?

settings.editor: The right solution depends on what you're noticing. If your home feels sticky, damp, or musty, humidity control may be the best place to start. If you're concerned about buildup inside your HVAC system, UV light purification may be worth considering. If dust, pollen, pet dander, or odors are the main issue, indoor purification may be the better fit.

Some homes need more than one solution. A home with high humidity and musty odors may need humidity control and HVAC maintenance. A home with seasonal allergy concerns may benefit from better filtration, indoor purification, and regular system care.
Air Comfort Services can evaluate your concerns, inspect key HVAC components, and explain your options clearly so you can make a confident decision.

settings.title: Indoor Air Quality Questions? We Have Answers

tabs.tab_title: What are signs that my home has poor indoor air quality?
tabs.tab_content: Common signs include excessive dust, musty odors, sticky air, allergy-like symptoms indoors, stale rooms, and humidity problems. A professional inspection can help identify what may be contributing to the issue.

tabs.tab_title: What is the best indoor air quality solution for my home?
tabs.tab_content: It depends on the concern. Humidity control can help with sticky air and moisture. UV light purification can support cleaner HVAC components. Indoor purification can help reduce airborne particles, odors, and allergens.

tabs.tab_title: Can humidity control help my AC work better?
tabs.tab_content: Humidity control can help your home feel more comfortable during humid Tri-Cities summers. When moisture is managed properly, your home may feel cooler without constantly lowering the thermostat.

tabs.tab_title: What does a UV light do in an HVAC system?
tabs.tab_content: UV lights are installed in certain areas of the HVAC system to help reduce biological buildup on compatible components. They are often used as part of a broader indoor air quality strategy.

tabs.tab_title: Is whole-home purification better than a portable air purifier?
tabs.tab_content: Whole-home purification can treat air moving through the HVAC system and provide broader coverage than a single-room portable unit. The best option depends on your home, system, and air quality concerns.
